correctness.rationale: The set of distinct rational tangent lines must cover PG(2,5), equivalently a dual blocking set. A COMPLETE independently rerun g++ integer enumeration of all binom(31,8)=7,888,725 eight-line subsets found 9,300 covering sets, all containing a full 6-line pencil. The classical nontrivial blocking-set lower bound of 9 applies to fewer-line covers; no 8-line non-pencil cover exists. Any putative smooth quartic with <=8 rational points has six pencil tangencies. Normalize their center to [0:0:1]; all 34,375 patterns (5^6+6*5^5) of chosen contact points lead to explicit 12×15 linear F5 quartic coefficient systems. Read and reran complete verify_pencil_lower.cpp: ranks {9:25,11:750,12:33600}, 912,000 rationally nonsingular solutions encountered, minimum rational point count 9. Rational nonsingularity is a weaker filter than geometric smoothness, so this excludes all smooth counterexamples without assuming exhaustive geometric-point tests. Separately used exact finite-field rational tangent checks and SymPy Groebner Jacobian unit ideals on each projective chart for both provided quartics: each has 9 rational points, 9 distinct tangents covering all 31 plane points, and the claimed pencil distinction. This is a complete bounded exact search, not an extrapolation.
residual_risks: The theorem is only F5 smooth quartics, not all finite fields or singular quartics.
The work does not classify all extremal projective quartic orbits; two incidence modes are witnessed.

evidence: Asgarli–Ghioca study tangent-filling curves over general finite fields and note their proposed degree-q−1 construction fails for q=5.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither stronger general statement alone covers the sharp smooth degree-four F5 minimum and its two extremal incidence modes.

value.rationale: The sharp minimum number of rational points for a geometrically smooth tangent-filling quartic over the smallest field q=5 at degree q−1 is a natural extremal question left open by broader construction bounds; the curve condition prevents generic blocking-set estimates from settling it. The two explicit smooth extremizers realize combinatorially distinct dual covering modes, making this a substantive complete finite classification of a sharp invariant rather than a random table entry. The full lower bound requires nontrivial exhaustive linear-algebra certificates.
residual_risks: Single field/degree only, and two examples do not classify all extremal quartics.

final_claim: Every geometrically smooth plane quartic over F5 whose rational tangents cover all 31 rational projective points has at least nine F5 points. Two explicit smooth nine-point quartics attain the bound with respectively a complete six-line rational tangent pencil and no complete rational pencil; not an exhaustive projective-class census.
limitations: The exact lower bound is based on exhaustive finite C++ searches independently rerun here; there is no short human-only inequality for the full-pencil case.
Geometric smoothness of witnesses was checked by three GF(5) Jacobian unit ideals; the lower-bound search tests a weaker rationally nonsingular superset.
An earlier unpublished/unindexed complete PG(2,5) tangent-filling curve census could contain this minimum or the explicit witnesses.
The claim deliberately omits exhaustive projective classification of all nine-point extremizers.
